steps.text: Cook ground beef, onion, mushrooms, garlic powder, and mustard powder in a large skillet over medium heat until beef is browned and crumbly, 6 to 8 minutes.

Sprinkle flour evenly over beef mixture and stir well until coated. Stir in beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, and black pepper, scraping up browned bits from the bottom of the skillet with a wooden spoon. Bring to a simmer and cook until slightly thickened, 10 to 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook egg noodles in a large pot of boiling salted water until tender, about 7 to 9 minutes; drain and keep warm.
Remove beef stroganoff from heat; carefully stir in sour cream until well blended and heated through. Serve over hot egg noodles and garnish with freshly chopped parsley.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Ground Beef Stroganoff
raw_recipe.description: This ground beef stroganoff recipe with mushrooms and sour cream is quick and easy to make in 30 minutes; serve over noodles for a family favorite.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Ground Beef Stroganoff

review.reviewBody: This has to be the best Stroganoff on earth. I did add 1 can cream of mushroom an upped the sour cream to 3/4 and the mayo down to a 1/4. This is so fast and simple to make let alone awesome. This is a must try! Thanks for this one it will definitely get used and passed on!

i don't understand the negative reviews here. obviously, this is not a gourmet recipe. but it is quick and filling comfort food that also happens to taste great, and is very easy to modify a bit here and there to suit your tastes. after i browned the beef, i rinsed it once to help eliminate grease. i browned the onions and mushrooms separately in a little butter, and i think that helped the flavor a lot. i increased the garlic powder a bit, and added a few dashes of dried dill. i decreased the mayo and increased the sour cream. also added just a bit of worchestershire sauce. although it doesn't look too spectacular, it tastes yummy!

This recipe is missing a key ingredient. You can not get an authentic strogenoff flavor without adding worchestershire sauce. It's the key to a great sauce. With that being said, here's what to omit -- the mayo. It's unnecessary and you don't need the mustard spice either. When you brown your beef, increase the garlic to 1 tsp. add in 1 tsp. of black pepper and 1 Tbsp. of worchestershire sauce. Your beef will get a savory flavor. In place of the mayo use 1 can cream of mushroom soup and decrease the beef stock to 1/4 cup. (I like to add an additional Tbsp. of worchestershire to the sauce.) Do not cover the sauce while simmering and it will thicken better.

Why anyone would spoil this by adding in a can of cream of soup with all its preservatives, namely MSG, is beyond me. If you feel it's "lacking", use spices, add more garlic, salt, pepper etc. I found as written, yes, a little lacking. I doubled it the next time, using fresh minced garlic, carmelizing my onions, salt and peppering them as they went into my pan, then adding in the minced garlic, about 6 cloves, in the last few seconds before I added the hamburger. I used a 16 ounce container of sour cream and half cup of Hellmans. I did use beef stock instead and to thicken it up slightly, I used 2 TBSP in 1/3 C milk. I also added about a TBSP or so of Worcestershire sauce to it. This is delicious!

Not bad, considering I don't particularly care for beef stroganoff. But this was a breeze! I did tweak it some. I doubled the recipe, using 2 lbs of ground beef and 1 lb of egg noodles. Hold the mayo and the broth, instead I used 8 oz of sour cream, 1 can of cream of mushroom soup, and powdered beef base. Watery sauce was not a problem this way. I also used double amounts of garlic, onion and mustard powders, as well as salt to taste and lots of black pepper, as nothing goes better with beef and noodles than black pepper. My husband wanted the noodles mixed in Hamburger Helper style, so we did that too. Yum!

Family Loved this! I, by habit, added ham seasoning to ground beef and used the advice of a reviewer to up the sour cream (12 oz), lower the mayo (2 TBLS) and added Worcestershire sauce (1 tsp). I, by habit again, added a can of green beans. My son's words; "this is better then hamburger helper Mom."

Cut mayo to 1/4 cup and increased sour cream to 3/4 cup, sautéed fresh mushrooms with the onion separately, then added the beef after draining it, also added Worcestershire sauce to cooking beef... next time would cut back a bit on the mustard.... overall delicious

This got rave reviews from my family (and me). Like other reviewers: I INcreased the sour cream by half and DEcreased the mayo by half. Used fresh mushrooms (sauteed separately in butter and stirred in about 1T flour, then added it all to the burger/cream mixture to thicken the sauce). Added quite a bit more dry mustard to taste. Also added worcestershire and salt/pepper to taste. Amazing, simple and something that will go on our regular rotation.

I'm giving this recipe 5 stars for it's versatility b/c I changed it quite a bit. Here's what I used:
1 lb. ground turkey
red wine
1/2 tbsp. dried mustard
1/4 tsp. minced garlic
1 can cream of mushroom soup
slightly less than 1/2 cup sour creme
1/2 cup fat free mayo
garlic salt/pepper to taste
worcestershire sauce
1/2 chopped onion
1/2 cup beef broth
appr. 3 tbsp. prepared horseradish
elbow macaroni

I browned the ground turkey with a splash of worcestershire sauce. I then drained and added the chopped onion, cooked for about 5 minutes. I combined the mustard, garlic, mayo, cream of mushroom soup, and beef broth. I added this to the beef/onion mixture and cooked for about 10 minutes. While this was cooking I cooked the elbow macaroni. About 3 minutes before I took off the beef mixture I added the horseradish and garlic salted/pepper to taste. Once the macaroni was cooked, I drained and combined. My family said it was the best stroganoff they ever tasted. I was very surprised and pleased that you couldn't taste the fat free mayo at all. I only changed the recipe b/c I didn't have all of the ingrediants. We were thrilled with the taste. Next time I'll use fat free sour cream and low fat cream of soup to make it a true low fat recipe.

Ok so this was great, I did make modifications but I usually do with meals. I add my twist- I did sub the mayo for sour cream 3/4 cup and 1/4 heavy cream. I added Worcestershire about two tsp. I added pepper and some onion chive mix salt from Trader Joe’s . I loved the beef broth idea and cut my own mushrooms to taste better. I didn’t do the onions because the hubs is allergic to fresh, but will next time to check taste- when he’s not available to eat. Kids loved it- hubby loved it. This serving size wasn’t enough for 4-6 I think more a 2-4 family size so I’ll double recipe next time. I had more noodles than sauce. But all in all a winner for something new!!

I made this with ground venison and also made a second one with a seafood medley. I used minced garlic instead of powdered. I added 1/2 cup of red bell peppers, 1/4 cup green onions. 1/2 cup of fresh parsley. fresh cut up mushrooms instead of canned.
Love it❣️
I added some broccoli instead of noodles for lower carbs.

Wonderful base recipe, especially when you’re looking for one without “cream of” soup. I add a little thyme and find it’s a perfect touch to an already good recipe. Don’t forget to season how YOU like it!
I quadrupled the recipe because I had 4lbs of ground beef. Instead of noodles I made mashed potatoes. Brought this into work and was a hit! Dan
Very bland tasting. Not enough sauce.
Good recipe easy to make and the kids love it.

I always ask my husband to rate all new recipes on a scale of 1-10, with 10 being excellent. He is typically a 7.5-9 “rater” and gave this one a 10!! He loves leftovers and also had it the next day for lunch and said, “this is REALLY good!”
Awesome
I added a tablespoon of Better than Beef bullion. Very good!
